payload.name: CompleteItemEnumerationWithVariedSearches
payload.description: When a question asks what books, movies, shows, or other items a person has read/watched/consumed, run multiple varied searches and inspect additional memories before answering, even if the first search returned some named items.
content: When a question asks for a list of items a person has read, watched, liked, or consumed (books, movies, series, foods, etc.), do not treat a single search that returns some named items as complete.

Before answering, run at least one additional hybrid or keyword search combining the subject's name with alternative activity terms and related subtypes (e.g., 'finished', 'enjoyed', 'mentioned', 'recommended', 'series', 'non-fiction', 'reads') to retrieve memories that name items without using the exact category noun.
Inspect both event and preference memories from these additional searches, and only produce the final list after no further varied search surfaces additional named items.

solves: For enumeration questions about a person's read/watched/consumed items, a single literal search is insufficient even if it returns some named items, because relevant memories may phrase items as 'finished a fantasy series' or 'enjoys non-fiction books'. The rule requires additional varied searches before answering. It applies to any item-list question (books, movies, shows, foods); it does not apply to single-item, yes/no, or count-only questions.
